questions.text: How would you prioritize a backlog when engineering capacity is fixed and every stakeholder thinks their request is P0?
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Prioritization framework (RICE/ICE), transparent criteria, stakeholder alignment.

questions.text: Walk me through how you'd define success metrics for a new feature before launch.
questions.ideal_answer_notes: North-star metric, leading vs lagging indicators, guardrail metrics.

questions.text: How would you decide whether to build, buy, or partner for a new capability?
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Cost/time tradeoffs, strategic differentiation, maintenance burden.

questions.text: Describe how you'd run and interpret an A/B test for a pricing change.
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Hypothesis, sample size/power, guardrail metrics, statistical vs practical significance.

questions.text: How do you scope an MVP for an ambiguous, high-uncertainty problem?
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Riskiest-assumption-first thinking, cutting scope without cutting value, fast feedback loops.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to say no to a feature request from a senior stakeholder.
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Diplomatic pushback, data-backed reasoning, relationship preserved.

questions.text: Describe a time a launch didn't go as planned. What did you do?
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Ownership, root-cause analysis, communication to stakeholders, concrete follow-up.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to align engineering, design, and sales around a single roadmap.
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Cross-functional facilitation, conflict resolution, shared success metric.

questions.text: Describe a decision you made with incomplete data. How did you decide, and how did it turn out?
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Structured judgment under uncertainty, willingness to revisit the decision.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you used customer feedback to change the direction of a product.
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Listening process, weighing feedback against strategy, measurable outcome.
